extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers / Scientific Review Group (SRG) members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for NIH Scientific Review Group members on pre-meeting, meeting, and post-meeting responsibilities and the criteria and procedures for evaluating NIH grant applications (overall impact, scored criteria, additional criteria, scoring and voting rules, and ethical obligations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written critique (use of templates and bullets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use critique templates provided by the SRO. Use bullets to note strengths and weaknesses for each of the scored review criteria and provide context and an explanation for your comments based on the project (e.g., refer to a Specific Aim). While brevity is acceptable, bullets should express complete thoughts and be sufficient to inform the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a paragraph summarizing the factors that informed your Overall Impact score. Download the critique templates and enter bulleted comments directly into the document (or paste as plain text to retain bullets). Upload the document to IAR. See the Critique Template Instructions for more information. Discussants may be asked to provide an 'Overall Impact' critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH scoring system (9-point scale; whole numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH scoring system uses a 9-point scale for the overall impact score and individual scores for (at least) five scored criteria. For both types of score, ratings are in whole numbers only (no decimal ratings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH expects that scores of 1 or 9 to be used less frequently than the other scores. 5 is considered an average score. Enter scores into IAR (not on the template). See the Scoring System and Procedure for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall impact score and critique to reflect your assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the five (or more) scored review criteria, and additional review criteria (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a paragraph summarizing the factors that informed your Overall Impact score. This paragraph should be a stand-alone assessment of the strengths and weaknesses outlined for each of the scored criteria and additional review criteria, not a restatement or summary of the specific aims or the bulleted comments. Basic and applied research are equally relevant. Unless stated otherwise in the FOA, an application does not need to be strong in all categories to be judged likely to have major scientific impact. The Overall Impact score is not necessarily the average of the individual criterion scores. For other activity codes (fellowships, career awards, training programs), overall impact may be defined differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criterion: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance is a core scored review criterion used to evaluate the scientific and technical merit of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how the project addresses an important problem or barrier in the field and the potential for the work to improve scientific knowledge, technical capability, or clinical practice. See 'Review Criteria at a Glance' for guidance specific to mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criterion: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s) is a scored review criterion focusing on the qualifications and expertise of the members of the research team for the work proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on qualifications and expertise including the Personal Statement in each Biosketch. Unless the application is for a fellowship or career development award, remarks about career tracks, titles, or salaries should be reserved for the Additional Comments to the Applicant box, or the Budget section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criterion: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation is a scored review criterion assessing whether the project uses novel concepts, approaches, or methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the application challenges current paradigms, introduces novel theoretical concepts, methodologies, or interventions, or refines/enhances existing approaches in a way that advances the field. See 'Review Criteria at a Glance' for mechanism-specific interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criterion: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach is a scored review criterion focused on the strategy, methodology, and analyses proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the rigor, feasibility, and appropriateness of the experimental design and methods, including potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success. Evaluate how well the approach addresses stated aims and whether the investigators have considered limitations and contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criterion: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment is a scored review criterion evaluating the institutional setting and resources available to support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the institutional support, facilities, and other resources will contribute to the probability of success. Assess mentorship or collaborative environments as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria (human subjects, vertebrate animals, SABV, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, consider the additional review criteria in the determination of scientific and technical merit and an overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not give separate scores for these items. Use the specific NIH guidance documents (e.g., review of Vertebrate Animals section; Human Subjects; Inclusion; Human Embryonic Stem Cells; Rigor and Transparency; SABV decision tree) for evaluation details. These elements (human subject protections, inclusion plans, vertebrate animals, biohazards) can affect scientific and technical merit and are discussed before final scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Considerations (budget, select agents, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, comment on each of the additional review considerations, but do not assign scores and do not consider these items when determining an overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff will administratively handle any concerns on these items following the review. See guidelines on Budget Information and Considering Information on Select Agents for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighing criteria and deriving Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Weigh the different criteria as you see fit in deriving your overall scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no formula used to derive the overall impact score from the individual criterion scores. Consider the relative strengths and weaknesses across criteria and the nature of the proposed work when determining overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score the application as presented (no assumed deletions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Score an application as presented in its entirety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not modify your scores on the assumption that a portion of the work proposed will be deleted or modified according to the SRG’s recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-meeting responsibilities (assignments, COI check, certifications, uploads)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine review assignments, review materials (including FOAs and applications), instructions, and review all applications pending review for conflict of interest or the appearance of conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you perceive a conflict or have questions, contact the SRO immediately. Review your assignments for match with your expertise and contact the SRO if concerns. Review the 'NIH Conflict of Interest Rules' and complete the NIH pre-review Certification. Sign the Confidentiality Certification (usually in the Internet Assisted Review module). Read, evaluate and write critiques for assigned applications, gain access to and upload critiques, preliminary overall impact scores and individual criterion scores to IAR by the deadline, and read posted critiques for assigned and other applications (access denied where you have a COI). Prepare for meeting discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer roles and mail reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: SRG members are designated as primary, secondary, or tertiary reviewers, and additional reviewers, as needed; mail reviewers; and discussants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All eligible SRG members with no conflict of interest participate in evaluation. Mail Reviewers do not attend the review meeting and their preliminary overall impact scores are not used to calculate the average preliminary or final score, though their critiques and scores are considered by the review panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting responsibilities: presentation and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned reviewers will share their initial overall impact score and should be prepared to explain the significance of the proposed research and the overall impact the research will have on the field. Group discussion follows assigned reviewer presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open discussion may result in disparate levels of enthusiasm; reasons for disparities should be made clear to allow for an informed vote and a high-quality summary statement. Elements such as human subject protections, inclusion plans, vertebrate animals or biohazards are discussed before final scoring because they can affect scientific and technical merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final scoring, voting, and numeric/non-numeric vote codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on presentation and discussion and preliminary critiques and overall impact scores, each discussed application is given a score by all reviewers eligible to vote on that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both regularly appointed and temporary members vote if eligible. You may use non-numeric impact scores: AB (abstain), CF (conflict of interest; did not participate), NP (not present). Committee decisions scenarios include ND (not discussed), NR (not recommended for further consideration), DF (deferred). If a particular score is an outlier, the reviewer must have stated concerns during the discussion so they can be reflected in the final summary statement. The scores from all eligible reviewers for a given application are averaged (calculated to one decimal point) and multiplied by 10 to determine the final overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-meeting edit phase and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: After the meeting, the SRO sets an 'Edit Phase' in IAR during which reviewers should edit criterion scores and critiques to reflect any changes to their preliminary assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must sign your post-meeting Conflict of Interest (COI) certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct: conflict of interest rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for potential conflicts of interest (or appearances of conflicts) and alert the SRO immediately. During the meeting, if you have a conflict of interest with any application or proposal, you must leave the room during evaluation and scoring of that application or proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In signing the post-review certification, you certify that you did not participate in an evaluation of any application or proposal with which you knowingly had a conflict of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct: confidentiality and handling of materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications and related materials are privileged communications that cannot be shown to or discussed with unauthorized individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited actions include sharing applications or materials with unauthorized persons, granting access to NIH secure systems or meetings to unauthorized persons, disclosing committee deliberations or evaluations to unauthorized persons or those with declared COI, and using information for personal benefit. By signing the confidentiality certification you certify understanding. You are required to leave all non-public review materials with the SRO or destroy them at the conclusion of the review meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Research misconduct is defined as fabrication, falsification, or plagiarism in proposing, performing, or reviewing research, or in reporting research results, but not honest error or differences of opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make allegations of potential misconduct in the critique or during the meeting discussion; instead, bring such concerns to the attention of the SRO in a confidential manner, preferably before the study section meets.
